column4: ## Building a Foundation that Lasts
column5: ## Building a Lasting Foundation

column4: I have always had a fascination with questions. Why is *something* true? What made it that way? How do we know? How are we sure? If *something* is true, what else is true? What is false? This fascination goes beyond a desire to be correct on a surface level, but to know deeply and precisely, and to be able to clearly articulate the new gained understanding.
column5: I have always been fascinated by questions. Why is *something* true? What made it so? How do we know? How are we certain? If *something* is true, what else is true? What is false? This interest goes beyond a mere desire to be superficially right; it is to know with depth and precision, and to have the ability to clearly express the new understanding gained.

column4: While communication is common, effective and precise communication is challenging. To effectively communicate a message the author and originator must have an idea. However, the idea alone like water on a hard surface-its edges and boundaries are poorly defined, fluid, and easily moved around.
column5: Although communication is common, effective and precise communication is challenging. To convey a message effectively, the author and originator must have an idea. However, an idea alone—like water on a hard surface—has vague edges and boundaries, is fluid, and is easily moved about.

column4: We use words, terms, and phrases to transform the raw idea from vaguely shaped to precisely shaped. Words give our idea a boundary, they help us distinguish and separate between what the idea is, and what it is not. Now our shaped idea must be transmitted and received through some medium. Whether in long form text, like this book, or short form text, like a social media post, or in oral form, like a conversation or a video recording, the medium transmits the now well-formed idea to the recipient.
column5: We use words, terms, and phrases to shape the raw idea from a vague form into a precise one. Words give our idea a boundary; they help us distinguish and differentiate what the idea is, and what it is not. Now our formed idea must be transmitted and received through some medium. Whether in long-form text, like this book, or in short-form text, like a social media post, or in spoken form, like a conversation or a video recording, the medium conveys this now formally shaped idea to the recipient.

column4: So far, we’ve only discussed the originator and author of the idea. For an idea to be useful, the recipient must receive, decode, and understand the message accurately. The transmitted and received messages should align closely.
column5: Up to this point, we have only spoken of the originator and author of the idea. For an idea to be useful, the recipient must accurately receive, decode, and understand the message. The sent and received messages must be closely aligned with each other.

column4: Every great human work is the by-product of effective communication. One man’s labor can only accomplish so much. To really build or perform something great, many men (speaking here generically of mankind) must labor together in a shared purpose, with a shared idea. Barring naturally occurring disasters (like a volcanic eruption) we also know that the greatest calamities to ever occur usually did so in significant part because of missing, broken or distorted communication. Truly life and death are in the power of the tongue (Proverbs 18:21).
column5: Every great human achievement is a byproduct of effective communication. One person’s labor can only go so far. To truly build or accomplish anything great, many people (in the broad sense of humanity) work together with a shared purpose and a common idea. Setting aside natural disasters (e.g., volcanic eruptions), we also know that the greatest catastrophes that have occurred were often largely due to lost, broken, or distorted communications. Indeed, life and death are in the power of the tongue (Proverbs 18:21).

column4: What we believe and how we communicate it has the power to build a person, a family, a community, a nation, or has the power to equally destroy them. What we believe is the foundation for our actions and is the blueprint for what we will do, who we will be, how we will exist. Because belief is expressed through action and communication, it defines the role we play in existence. Our beliefs shape not just our lives, but to a degree the lives of everyone around us.

Since faith is manifested through action and communication, it defines the role we play in existence. column4: Many Christians today desire a stronger faith but lack a clear foundation to build upon. Without solid doctrine, we lack the firm foundation we need to stand strong; we risk being swayed by false teaching, discouraged in trials, or unprepared for the work God has called us to do. This book is designed to equip you with the foundational teachings of Scripture-truths that strengthen your faith, deepen your walk with Christ, and empower you to live a Spirit-filled life.

column5: ## Why this book, and for whom?

column4: The teachings in this book are meant to educate and encourage you, the reader, in the foundational doctrines of the New Testament church. It is my hope that these beliefs will convince and inspire your walk of faith to plant deep roots in Christ and to come to know Him personally.
column5: The teachings of this book are intended to instruct and encourage you, the reader, in the foundational doctrines of the New Covenant Church. column4: These teachings are framed and shaped by my experience in the church, particularly in Charismatic or Pentecostal manifestations. These writings, divinely inspired, were carefully recorded, compiled, and preserved through the centuries, forming what is now known as the Bible.

These writings, which were divinely inspired, were carefully recorded, collected, and preserved over the centuries, and thus the collection was formed which is now called the Bible.
